=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_head_gate.sh: `review_head_gate_freshness_sync`, the parent, `web-flow` committer, `verified` and compare checks | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The code says GitHub's signature means "no one edited" the merge. It does not. The checks cover only parentage (first parent is `from`, second parent is on the base), committer (`web-flow`) and signature. None of them constrain the commit's tree. A merge commit made through GitHub's web conflict editor, or through the Merges API, passes all four checks. It is signed by `web-flow`, has the approved head as first parent and the base tip as second parent, and its tree can still contain hand-edited content. Such a head skips the reviewer panel and goes to `deterministic-skip-merge`, which runs no reviewers and no single-issue security pass. Two preconditions apply: a trusted marker for the approved head must already exist, and the actor must be a same-repo writer. The conflict-editor route also needs the PR to have conflicted first.
  WHY: The reviewers are skipped for a head whose content was not produced by a clean base merge. The risk is small, because it requires write access and a prior marker. The stated invariant is still stronger than what the code enforces. A cheap, stricter test is possible: require `compare/<from>...<head>` to list only files that also appear in the base-side diff. The alternative is to soften the comment and the docs to say what is actually verified.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: `gate_freshness_sync_fast_path`, lines ~1314-1316, against the `AUTOFIX_SKIP_SUPPRESS_ON_CONFLICT` check at ~1677 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fast path suppresses on `mergeable=false` or `dirty` unconditionally, while the doc-only / small-diff skip honours `AUTOFIX_SKIP_SUPPRESS_ON_CONFLICT=false`. With that variable set to `false`, a conflicted PR still takes the normal review path instead of the skip, so the variable's documented behaviour does not reach this skip.
  WHY: Nothing breaks. The divergence is in the safe direction, because the in-run conflict resolver handles the PR. The existing "no repo variable names are renamed" contract is unaffected. This is an accepted residual from the previous round.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh (`_pr_base_sync_count`) and scripts/review_head_gate.sh (`review_head_gate_freshness_sync`)
  location: the marker regex match
  issue: Both place no check on the comment prefix. Any comment by the workflow login that ends with the marker text counts, and editor summaries carry text that PR content can influence.
  suggested minimal fix: also require the body to start with "**Branch updated from `" in both places, for example `select(startswith("**Branch updated from `"))`.
  estimated lines changed: 2
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: NONE

=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh: 753 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The code uses `_safe_gh_jq -X POST` to write a marker comment.
  WHY: `_safe_gh_jq` is designed for read-only, audit-protected operations. Using it for POST requests may bypass or be incompatible with the repository's security/audit model for write operations.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh: 753-756 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: If the marker comment POST fails, the branch update is accepted but not recorded in the sync history.
  WHY: Subsequent freshness checks will not count this update towards the MERGE_BASE_FRESHNESS_MAX_SYNCS cap, potentially allowing the branch to exceed the configured update limit and defeating the purpose of the cap.

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh (`_pr_base_sync_marker_post`)
  Location: marker-body filter in `_pr_base_sync_count` and the body capture in `review_head_gate.sh freshness-sync`
  Issue: A comment counts as a marker only by author-login and a regex anchored at the end of the body. A pipeline-authored comment (e.g., editor summary) that ends with the marker-shaped text — even if its body has nothing to do with a merge-base sync — would be counted, and (when followed by GitHub's signed merge of the approved head) trusted to skip the reviewer panel.
  Suggested minimal fix: also require the body to start with `**Branch updated from \`` in both `_pr_base_sync_count` and the gate's `capture()` filter (mirror the "Branch updated from `%s`" prefix the marker producer always writes).
  Estimated lines changed: 4 (two jq `test()` calls plus the corresponding `capture()` literal updates in `review_head_gate.sh`).
- File: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Location: `gate_freshness_sync_fast_path` (the LAST RUN DIFF block at lines ~1313-1322) vs the doc-only/small-diff skip's copy of the same single-issue-security-pass suppressor at ~lines 1688-1692.
  Issue: The single-issue-security-pass eligibility rule now lives in two byte-similar inline copies in the same gate job. The wiring test (`tests/test_pr_base_freshness_gate.py::FreshnessSyncWiring`) only checks the fast-path copy; nothing ties the two copies together. A future change that updates one copy (e.g., adds a label exemption) and misses the other could let a security-pass-eligible PR take the fast path and merge unaudited.
  Suggested minimal fix: extend `FreshnessSyncWiring` with one assertion that the exact five-line eligibility block also appears verbatim in the doc-only/skip block, or extract the eligibility into one bash helper both paths call.
  Estimated lines changed: 6 (a single `assertIn` for each of the four condition lines, plus an ordering check).
- The pre-existing concerns from pass 1 (printf format-string safety, `_safe_gh_jq -X POST` compatibility, marker-write idempotency) are either unfounded — the format string has exactly 10 `%s` matching 10 arguments and `_safe_gh_jq` is the standard API helper used for both reads and writes elsewhere (e.g., `update-branch` PUT) — or already addressed by the LAST RUN DIFF: switching the marker POST from `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq` to a single-attempt `_safe_gh_jq` exactly resolves the duplicate-marker risk and matches the inline comment that names the failure mode. No new runtime defects were introduced by the LAST RUN DIFF.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh: 752-756, 784-785; marker count at 723-727 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A successful branch update is not recorded when posting its marker comment fails. The failure path only warns, while the per-PR cap counts marker comments.
  WHY: If GitHub accepts the branch update but the comment POST fails, the next freshness check can read the comments successfully and count no marker. It then permits another update, exceeding MERGE_BASE_FRESHNESS_MAX_SYNCS and repeating the review cycle the cap is intended to limit.

=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh: `_pr_base_sync_marker_post` at lines 752-756; `_pr_base_fresh_for_merge` at lines 783-786 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the branch update succeeds but the marker comment POST fails, the code logs a warning and returns 0 without recording that accepted update. The cap counter `_pr_base_sync_count` will not see that update on the next freshness check.
  WHY: If the base moves under the PR again before the next synchronize run, the gate will count 0 markers for that update, attempt another update-branch call, and the per-PR cap can be exceeded by one. The cross-pollination finding from openai_gpt-6-luna identified this. The autofix already removed the `gh_retry` wrapper to prevent duplicate markers on retry, which addresses the worse direction; the remaining failure mode (transient comment-write failure) is rare and the consequence is one extra review cycle, not an incorrect merge.

=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
